7:2: A Book sent down to you, so let there not be in your breast any distress on account of it, that you may warn with it and as an admonition for the believers.
7:3: Follow what has been sent down to you from your Rabb, and do not follow protectors besides Him. How little you take heed!
7:4: And how many cities We destroyed, and Our punishment came upon them at night or while they were taking a midday rest.
7:5: When Our punishment came to them, their supplication was nothing but to say, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
7:6: And surely We will question those to whom [messengers] were sent, and surely We will question the messengers as well.
7:7: And surely We will narrate to them with a knowledge, and We were not absent.
7:8: And the weighing on that Day is the truth; whose scales are heavy, then those are the ones who are saved.
7:9: And whose scales are light, then those are the ones who have brought ruin to their souls because they wronged Our verses.
7:10: And surely We established you in the earth and made for you therein means of livelihood; little do you give thanks.
7:11: And surely We created you, then We shaped you, then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis.
7:12: Allah said: What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you? Iblis said: I am better than him. You created me from fire, and him You created from clay.
7:13: He said: Then descend from there, for it is not for you to be arrogant there. Get out; indeed, you are of the humiliated ones.
7:14: Iblis said: Give me respite until the day they are resurrected.
7:15: Allah said: Indeed, you are of those given respite.
7:16: He said: Because You led me astray, surely I will sit in wait against them on Your straight path.
7:17: Then I will come to them from before them, from behind them, from their right, and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful.
7:18: Allah said: Get out of there, disgraced and expelled. Whoever of them follows you, I will surely fill Hell with all of you.
7:19: O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you be of the wrongdoers.
7:20: Then Satan whispered to them that he might reveal to them what was hidden from them of their shameful parts. And he said: Your Rabb forbade you this tree only lest you become two angels or become of those who abide eternally.
7:21: And he swore to them: Indeed, I am surely of the sincere advisers to the two of you.
7:22: Thus he caused them to fall through deception. When they tasted of the tree, their shameful parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of Paradise. And their Rabb called out to them: 'Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is an open enemy to you?'
7:23: The two said: Our Rabb, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.
7:24: Allah said: Descend as enemies to one another. And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and a livelihood for a time.
7:25: He said: Therein you live, and therein you die, and from it you will be brought out.
7:26: O Children of Adam, We have sent down to you a garment to cover your shameful parts and as an adornment. And the garment of taqwa is better. That is from the verses of Allah, so that they may take heed.
7:27: O Children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you, just as he expelled your parents from Paradise, stripping them of their garments to show them their shameful parts. Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe.
7:28: When they commit an ugly deed, they say: We found our fathers upon this, and Allah commanded us with it. Say: Indeed, Allah does not command ugliness.
7:29: Say: My Rabb commanded justice, and keep your faces upright at every masjid, and supplicate to Him, making religion purely for Him. As He created you initially, you shall return.
7:30: A party He guided, and upon a party error was justified. Indeed, they took devils as allies instead of Allah, and they think that they are rightly guided.
7:31: O Children of Adam! Take your adornment at every masjid, and eat and drink, and do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not love those who are extravagant.
7:32: Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants and the good things of provision? Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world, and purely for them on the Day of Resurrection. Thus We explain the verses for a people who know.
7:33: Say: My Rabb has only forbidden indecencies—what is apparent of them and what is concealed—and sin, and unjust oppression, and that you associate with Allah that for which He sent down no authority, and that you say concerning Allah that which you do not know.
7:34: And for every nation there is an appointed term; when their term comes, they cannot delay it by even an hour, nor can they advance it.
7:35: O Children of Adam! When messengers come to you from among yourselves narrating to you My verses, whoever guards against evil and reforms, then there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
7:36: As for those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them, they are the companions of the Fire. They will abide eternally therein.
7:37: Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His verses? Those, their share from the Book will reach them. Until when Our messengers come to them to take their souls, they say: Where are those whom you used to invoke besides Allah? They say: They have abandoned us. And they testify against themselves that they were disbelievers.
7:38: He says: Enter into the Fire among communities of jinn and humans that have passed away before you. Whenever a community enters, it curses its sister community. Until when they have all gathered there, the later ones say concerning the earlier ones: Our Rabb! These are the ones who led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire. He says: For each there is double, but you do not know.
7:39: And the earlier ones say to the later ones: You had no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn.
7:40: Indeed, for those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them, the gates of heaven will not be opened, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle; and thus We recompense the criminals.
7:41: For them is a bed of Hell and over them are coverings, and thus We recompense the wrongdoers.
7:42: Those who believe and do righteous deeds—We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity—those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide eternally therein.
7:43: We removed what was in their chests of rancor, rivers flow beneath them. They say: 'Praise be to Allah, who guided us to this. If Allah had not guided us, we could not have found guidance. By oath, the messengers of our Rabb brought the truth.' And it is called out to them: 'This is the Paradise that has been made your inheritance, in return for what you used to do.'
7:44: The people of Paradise call out to the people of Hell: 'We found what our Rabb promised us to be true. Did you also find what your Rabb promised you to be true?' They say: 'Yes.' Thereupon a caller calls out among them: 'The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.'
7:45: They are those who hinder from the path of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they are those who deny the Hereafter.
7:46: Between the two of them is a veil. On the A'raf are men who recognize everyone by their marks. They call out to the people of Paradise: 'Peace be upon you!' They have not yet entered it, but they hope.
7:47: When their eyes are turned toward the people of the Fire, they say: 'Our Rabb, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.'
7:48: The people of the A'raf call out to men whom they recognize by their marks: 'Your gathering and what you used to act arrogantly about did not benefit you.'
7:49: Were these the ones whom you swore that Allah would not extend mercy to? Enter Paradise; there is no fear for you, nor will you grieve.
7:50: The people of the Fire call out to the people of Paradise: 'Pour some water upon us or some of what Allah has provided for you as sustenance.' They say: 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers.'
7:51: Those who took their religion as amusement and play, and the worldly life deceived them. Today We forget them just as they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs and as they used to deny Our verses.
7:52: By oath, We brought them a book; We explained it upon a knowledge, as a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.
7:53: Do they wait for anything other than its interpretation? The day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: 'The messengers of our Rabb had indeed come with the truth. Now, are there any intercessors for us who will intercede? Or could we be sent back so that we might do deeds other than what we used to do?' Indeed, they brought loss upon themselves, and what they used to invent was lost from them.
7:54: Indeed, your Rabb is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself above the Arsh. He covers the night with the day, which pursues it swiftly. He has subjected the sun, the moon, and the stars by His command. Beware, creation and command belong to Him. How exalted is Allah, the Rabb of the worlds.
7:55: Pray to your Rabb beseechingly and secretly. Indeed, He does not like those who transgress the limits.
7:56: Do not make corruption on the earth after its reformation, and pray to Him with fear and hope. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.
7:57: It is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy; finally, when they bear heavy clouds, We drive it to a dead land and send down water with it and bring forth thereby all kinds of fruits; thus We bring forth the dead as well, that perhaps you may take heed.
7:58: The vegetation of the good land comes forth with the permission of its Rabb, while that which is bad comes forth only with difficulty; thus We explain the verses for a people who give thanks.
7:59: By oath, We sent Noah as a messenger to his people. He said: 'O my people! Worship Allah; there is no deity for you other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.'
7:60: The notables from his people said: "Indeed, we see you in clear error."
7:61: He said: "O my people! There is no error in me. Rather, I am a messenger from the Rabb of the worlds."
7:62: I convey to you the messages of my Rabb, I give you advice, and I know from Allah what you do not know.
7:63: Did you wonder that an admonition has come to you from your Rabb through a man from among yourselves, so that he may warn you, and that you may be mindful, and that perhaps you may receive mercy?
7:64: They denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We drowned those who denied Our verses; indeed, they were a blind people.
7:65: And to the people of Ad We sent their brother Hud. He said: "O my people! Worship Allah. There is no deity for you other than Him. Will you not still be mindful?"
7:66: The notables who disbelieved from his people said: "Indeed, we see you in foolishness, and indeed, we think you are of the liars."
7:67: He said: "O my people! There is no foolishness in me. Rather, I am a messenger from the Rabb of the worlds."
7:68: I convey to you the messages of my Rabb, and I am a trustworthy adviser for you.
7:69: Did you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Rabb through a man from among yourselves to warn you? Remember that He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in stature in creation, so that perhaps you may attain salvation.
7:70: They said: 'Did you come to us so that we worship Allah alone and leave what our ancestors worshipped? If you are of the truthful, bring us that which you promise us.'
7:71: He said: "A filth and a wrath from your Rabb has definitely fallen upon you. Do you dispute with me about names which you and your ancestors have named, for which Allah has sent down no proof? Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait."
7:72: Thus We saved him and those with him by a mercy from Us, and We cut off the roots of those who denied Our verses.
7:73: And to the people of Thamud We sent their brother Salih. He said: "O my people! Worship Allah. There is no deity for you other than Him. A clear proof has come to you from your Rabb. Here is this she-camel of Allah, a sign for you. Leave her alone to eat in Allah's earth. Do not touch her with harm, or else a painful punishment will seize you."
7:74: Remember that He made you successors after the people of Ad and settled you in the earth; you take mansions from its plains and carve homes from the mountains. So remember the blessings of Allah, and do not cause disorder making corruption on the earth.
7:75: The notables who were arrogant from his people said to those who were oppressed among those who believed: "Do you really know that Salih has been sent from his Rabb?"
7:76: Those who were arrogant said: 'Indeed, we are disbelievers in that which you believe.'
7:77: Thereupon they hamstrung the she-camel and grew arrogant against the command of their Rabb and said: "O Salih! If you are of the messengers, bring us that which you promise us."
7:78: Thereupon, a tremor seized them, and they became fallen prone on their knees in their dwellings.
7:79: He turned away from them and said: 'O my people, I conveyed the message of my Rabb to you and gave you counsel, but you do not like those who give counsel.'
7:80: And Lot, when he said to his people: 'Do you commit the immorality that no one from the worlds has done before you?'
7:81: Indeed, you approach men with lust instead of women. Rather, you are a transgressing people.
7:82: The answer of his people was only that they said: 'Drive them out of your village, for they are people who want to cleanse themselves.'
7:83: So We saved him and his family, except his wife became of those who remained behind.
7:84: And We rained down rain upon them. Look, how was the end of the criminals?
7:85: And to Midian We sent their brother Shuaib. He said: 'O my people, worship Allah; there is no deity for you other than Him. A clear proof has come to you from your Rabb. Make the measure and the balance full, do not diminish people's belongings, and do not cause corruption in the earth after its reformation. If you are believers, this is better for you.'
7:86: And do not sit on every path threatening and barring from the way of Allah those who believe, trying to make it crooked. And remember that you were few and He multiplied you. Look, how was the end of the corrupters?
7:87: If a group among you has believed in what was sent with me and a group has not believed, be patient until Allah judges between us. He is the best of judges.
7:88: The notables of his people who were arrogant said: 'O Shuaib, we will definitely expel you and those who believe with you from our village, or else you will return to our religion.' He said: 'Even if we are unwilling?'
7:89: If we return to your religion after Allah has saved us from it, we would have fabricated a lie against Allah. It is not fitting for us to return to it unless Allah, our Rabb, wills. Our Rabb has encompassed everything in His knowledge. In Allah we have placed our trust. Our Rabb, judge between us and our people with truth. You are the best of judges.
7:90: The notables among his people who disbelieved said: 'If you follow Shuaib, then you will certainly be among the losers.'
7:91: Thereupon, a tremor seized them, and they became fallen prone on their knees in their dwellings.
7:92: Those who denied Shuaib became as if they had never lived there in prosperity; those who denied Shuaib, it was they who were the losers.
7:93: He turned away from them and said: 'O my people, I conveyed the messages of my Rabb to you and gave you counsel. Now how can I grieve over a disbelieving people?'
7:94: We did not send a prophet to a town without seizing its people with adversity and hardship, so that perhaps they might plead.
7:95: Then We replaced the evil with the good, until finally they pardoned and said: 'Adversity and abundance had touched our fathers too.'
7:96: If the people of the cities had believed and guarded themselves, We would surely have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth, but they denied.
7:97: Then did the people of the cities feel secure from Our punishment coming upon them at night while they were sleeping?
7:98: Or did the people of those cities feel secure from Our punishment coming upon them in mid-morning while they were playing?
7:99: Did they feel secure from Allah's trap? None feels secure from Allah's trap except the people who are losers.
7:100: Does it not make clear to those who inherit the earth after its previous owners that if We willed, We could strike them because of their sins?
7:101: Those are the cities whose news We relate to you. By oath, their messengers had come to them with clear proofs, yet they were not going to believe in what they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers.
7:102: We did not find any covenant in most of them, and We found most of them to be transgressors.
7:103: Then after them We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his notables, and they wronged them. Look, how was the end of the corrupters.
7:104: Moses said: 'O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Rabb of the worlds.'
7:105: It is an obligation upon me not to say about Allah except the truth; I have come to you with a clear proof from your Rabb, so send the Children of Israel with me.
7:106: He said: 'If you have come with a sign, bring it, if you are of the truthful.'
7:107: Thereupon, he threw his staff, and it became a manifest serpent.
7:108: And he drew out his hand, and thereupon it became pure white to the beholders.
7:109: The notables of Pharaoh's people said: 'Indeed, this is a learned sorcerer.'
7:110: He wants to drive you out of your land, so what do you command?
7:111: They said: 'Hold off him and his brother, and send gatherers to the cities.'
7:112: Let them bring you every learned sorcerer.
7:113: The sorcerers came to Pharaoh; they said: 'Indeed, if we are the victors, there is surely a reward for us.'
7:114: He said: 'Yes, and indeed you will be of those brought near.'
7:115: They said: 'O Moses, either you throw, or we will be the ones who throw.'
7:116: He said: 'Throw!' When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people, terrified them, and came with a great magic.
7:117: And We inspired to Moses: 'Throw your staff,' and suddenly it was swallowing what they fabricated.
7:118: Thus the truth was established, and what they were doing became void.
7:119: There they were defeated, and they turned back brought low.
7:120: The sorcerers were thrown down in prostration.
7:121: They said: "We have believed in the Rabb of the worlds."
7:122: The Rabb of Moses and Aaron.
7:123: Pharaoh said: 'Did you believe in him before I gave you permission? Indeed, this is a plot you devised in the city to drive its people out of it. But soon you will know.'
7:124: I will surely cut off your hands and your feet alternately, then I will surely crucify you all.
7:125: They said: "Indeed, we will only return to our Rabb."
7:126: You are taking revenge on us only because we believed in the signs of our Rabb when they came to us. Our Rabb, pour down patience upon us and cause us to die as Muslims.
7:127: The notables of Pharaoh's people said: "Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the earth and to forsake you and your gods?"
7:128: Moses said to his people: "Seek help from Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He makes whom He wills of His servants inherit it. And the end is for the possessors of taqwa."
7:129: They said: "We were tormented both before you came to us and after you came to us." He said: "It may be that your Rabb will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the earth, and see how you act."
7:130: And certainly We seized Pharaoh's family with years and diminution of crops so that perhaps they would take heed.
7:131: Whenever good came to them, they said, 'This is our right.' And if an evil befell them, they saw an ill omen in Moses and those with him.
7:132: And they said: "Whatever sign you bring to us in order to bewitch us with it, we are not going to believe in you."
7:133: Thereupon We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood as distinct signs; yet they were arrogant and they were a guilty people.
7:134: When the punishment fell upon them, they said: "O Moses, pray for us to your Rabb by virtue of His covenant with you. If you remove the punishment from us, we will certainly believe you and we will send the Children of Israel with you."
7:135: But when We removed the punishment from them until a term they were to reach, they immediately broke their word.
7:136: Thereupon We took retribution from them, and because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them, We drowned them in the sea.
7:137: And We made the people who were deemed weak inherit the easts and the wests of the land in which We placed blessings. And the good word of your Rabb was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were making and what they were erecting.
7:138: We made the Children of Israel cross the sea. Then they came upon a people devoted to idols that belonged to them. They said: 'O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods.' He said: 'Indeed, you are an ignorant people.'
7:139: Indeed, that which they are in is destroyed, and what they have been doing is vain.
7:140: He said: 'Shall I seek a god for you other than Allah, while He has favored you over the worlds?'
7:141: And when We saved you from Pharaoh's family; they were afflicting you with the worst punishment, slaughtering your sons and letting your women live, and in that was a great trial from your Rabb.
7:142: And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the time appointed by his Rabb was completed as forty nights, and Moses said to his brother Aaron: 'Take my place among my people, reform, and do not follow the path of the corrupters.'
7:143: When Moses came to Our appointed time and his Rabb spoke to him, he said: 'My Rabb, appear to me so that I may look at You.' He said: 'You can never see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me.' When his Rabb manifested Himself to the mountain, He crushed it to pieces, and Moses fell unconscious. When he regained consciousness, he said: 'Glory be to You, I have repented to You and I am the first of the believers.'
7:144: He said: 'O Moses, I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My speech. So take what I have given you and be of the grateful.'
7:145: And We wrote for him on the tablets an admonition concerning everything and the detail of everything; [saying:] take it with strength and command your people to take the best of it.
7:146: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right. Even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. If they see the right path, they will not adopt it as a path. But if they see the path of transgression, they will adopt it as a path. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
7:147: The deeds of those who deny Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter have come to nothing. They will only be recompensed for what they have been doing.
7:148: The people of Moses took, after him, from their ornaments a statue of a calf that lowed; did they not see that it did not speak to them and did not guide them to a path? They took it and became wrongdoers.
7:149: When it was fallen into their hands [with remorse] and they saw that they had indeed gone astray, they said: 'If our Rabb does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we shall certainly be among the losers.'
7:150: When Moses returned to his people, angry and sorrowful, he said: 'What an evil thing you did after me! Did you hasten the command of your Rabb?' He threw down the tablets and seized his brother by his head, dragging him toward himself. His brother said: 'O son of my mother, the people deemed me weak and almost killed me. So do not let the enemies rejoice over me and do not place me with the wrongdoing people.'
7:151: He said: 'My Rabb, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy. You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.'
7:152: Indeed, those who took the calf, wrath from their Rabb and humiliation in the life of this world will reach them. And thus do We recompense those who invent falsehoods.
7:153: As for those who committed evil deeds, then repented after that and believed, indeed, your Rabb after that is certainly Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
7:154: When the anger subsided from Moses, he took the tablets, and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Rabb.
7:155: Moses chose seventy men from his people for Our appointed time. When the earthquake seized them, he said: "My Rabb, if You had willed, You would have destroyed them and me before. Will You destroy us because of what the foolish among us have done? This is only Your trial; with it You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Wali (Protector), so forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are the Best of those who forgive."
7:156: And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter. Indeed, we have turned to You. He said: 'My punishment—I strike with it whom I will. And My mercy encompasses all things. I will decree it for those who have taqwa, give zakat, and believe in Our signs.'
7:157: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered (ummi) Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. He enjoins upon them what is right, forbids them what is wrong, makes lawful for them the clean things, makes unlawful for them the filthy things, and removes from them their heavy burdens and the shackles that were upon them. So those who believe in him, honor him, help him, and follow the light sent down with him, it is they who are the truly prosperous.
7:158: Say: "O people! Indeed, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all. He, to Whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but Him. He gives life and causes death. So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered (ummi) Prophet, who believes in Allah and His words. And follow him so that you may be guided."
7:159: And from the people of Moses is a community who guide according to the truth and establish justice with it.
7:160: And We divided them into twelve tribes, communities. And We revealed to Moses when his people asked him for water: "Strike the stone with your staff." From it gushed twelve springs. Every group knew its drinking place. And We made the clouds a canopy over them, and We sent down upon them manna and quails. "Eat from the clean things of what We have provided you as sustenance," We said. And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging their own selves.
7:161: And when it was said to them: 'Dwell in this town, eat from it wherever you wish, say "forgive", and enter the gate prostrating so that We may forgive your mistakes. And to those who do good, We will increase.'
7:162: But those who wronged among them replaced the word that had been said to them with another word. Thereupon We sent down upon them a punishment from heaven because they were doing wrong.
7:163: And ask them about that town which was by the sea, when they transgressed on the Sabbath, when on the Sabbath days their fish came to them openly, and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath they did not come to them; thus We tested them because they were defying.
7:164: And when a community among them said: "Why do you preach to a people whom Allah will destroy or punish with a severe punishment?" They said: "So that it may be an excuse to your Rabb, and perhaps they may guard themselves."
7:165: When they forgot what had been reminded to them, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who wronged with a severe punishment because they were acting defiantly.
7:166: So when they arrogantly exceeded that which they had been forbidden from, We said to them: 'Be despised apes.'
7:167: And your Rabb proclaimed that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, people who would make them taste an evil punishment. Surely your Rabb is very swift in retribution, and He is forgiving, merciful.
7:168: And We divided them on the earth into communities. Among them were the righteous, and among them were those other than that. And We tested them with good things and bad things, so that perhaps they might return.
7:169: Then after them succeeded a generation who inherited the Book; they take the fleeting goods of this vile world and say, 'We will be forgiven.' And if similar fleeting goods come to them, they take that too. Was the covenant on the Book not taken from them that they should not say about Allah anything except the truth? And they studied what is in it. The home of the Hereafter is better for those who guard themselves. Will you still not use your intellect?
7:170: Those who hold firmly to the Book and establish the salah; surely We do not waste the reward of those who reform.
7:171: And when We raised the mountain over them like a canopy and they thought that it was going to fall upon them: 'Hold firmly to what We have given you and remember what is in it so that you may guard yourselves,' He said.
7:172: Remember when your Rabb took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify over their own selves, saying: 'Am I not your Rabb?'
7:173: Or lest you say: 'Surely our fathers associated partners before, and we were a progeny that came after them; will You now destroy us because of what the doers of falsehood did?'
7:174: Thus We explain the verses so that perhaps they may return.
7:175: Recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our verses. He stripped himself away and distanced himself from the verses, then Satan pursued him, and thus he became of the deviants.
7:176: If We had willed, We would have elevated him with those verses. But he inclined toward the earth and followed his desire. His case is like the case of the dog: if you attack him, he lolls his tongue out; and if you leave him alone, he lolls his tongue out. This is the example of the people who denied Our verses. So relate the story; it is hoped that they will reflect.
7:177: How evil is the condition of the people who denied Our verses and were wronging their own selves.
7:178: Whomever Allah guides, he is the one who is guided. And whomever He leads astray, they are the losers.
7:179: And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humans. They have hearts with which they do not understand; they have eyes with which they do not see; they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like animals, indeed they are even more astray. Those are the very negligent ones.
7:180: The most beautiful names belong to Allah, so supplicate to Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His names.
7:181: And among those We have created is a community who guide with truth and establish justice with it.
7:182: As for those who deny Our verses, We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know.
7:183: I grant them respite. Surely My scheme is firm.
7:184: Have they not reflected that there is nothing of madness in the person who is their companion; he is only a clear warner.
7:185: Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and whatever thing Allah has created, and that perhaps their term might indeed have approached? After that, in what word will they believe?
7:186: Whomever Allah leads astray, there is no one to guide him anymore, and He leaves them wandering blindly in their transgression.
7:187: They ask you about the Hour of the Resurrection, when it will cast anchor. Say: 'Its knowledge is only with my Rabb. None will reveal it at its time except Him. It has weighed heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will come to you only suddenly.' They ask you as if you were well-informed of it. Say: 'Its knowledge is only with Allah. But most of the people do not know.'
7:188: Say: I possess no power to cause benefit or harm to myself, except what Allah wills. If I had known the unseen, I would surely have multiplied the good and no evil would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bearer of glad tidings for a people who believe.
7:189: He is the One who created you from a single soul and brought forth its mate from it so that he might find comfort in her. When he covered her, she carried a light burden and went about with it. When she grew heavy, they both prayed to their Rabb, Allah: 'If You give us a righteous child, we will surely be of the grateful.'
7:190: When He gave them a righteous child, they set up partners to Him in what He had given them. Allah is exalted above what they associate as partners.
7:191: Do they associate as partners things that create nothing, while they themselves are created?
7:192: And they are not able to give them help, nor can they help themselves.
7:193: If you call them to guidance, they will not follow you; it is all the same for you whether you have called them or you remain silent.
7:194: Surely those you worship besides Allah are servants like you; so call upon them, and let them respond to you if you are truthful.
7:195: Do they have feet with which they walk? Or do they have hands with which they hold? Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear? Say: 'Call your partners, then plot against me and do not give me respite.'
7:196: Indeed, my wali is Allah, who sent down the Book, and He takes the righteous as wali.
7:197: And those you call upon besides Him are not able to help you, nor do they help their own selves.
7:198: And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear. And you see them looking at you, yet they do not see.
7:199: Take forgiveness, command al-maruf, and turn away from the ignorant.
7:200: And if an impulse from Satan touches you, then immediately seek refuge in Allah; because He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
7:201: Indeed, those who guard, when a touch from Satan touches them, they remember, and immediately they become seeing.
7:202: And their brothers extend them in error, then they do not cut short.
7:203: And when you do not bring them an ayah, they say: 'Why did you not choose it?' Say: 'I only follow what is revealed to me from my Rabb. This is insights, guidance and mercy from your Rabb for a people who believe.'
7:204: And when the Quran is read, listen to it and be silent so that you may be shown mercy.
7:205: And remember your Rabb within your self, supplicating and in fear, other than what is open of speech, morning and evening, and do not be among the heedless.
7:206: Indeed, those who are in the presence of your Rabb are not too proud to serve Him, they glorify Him, and they prostrate to Him.
